quotes.text: Configuration is what you told the platform to do on a Tuesday afternoon. Control is what the platform does on a Friday night when a contractor shares a folder, a maker publishes a flow, a new copilot feature rolls out with defaults you didn't review.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise image that separates configured intent from actual system behavior in a tenant.

quotes.text: People love to treat ownership as metadata. It isn't. Ownership is an operational circuit. It is the difference between this looks risky and this gets fixed.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames ownership as the primitive that turns findings into fixes.

quotes.text: This is why label coverage can rise while risk rises. You've improved metadata. You haven't improved access boundaries.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why sensitivity labels alone do not reduce oversharing risk.

quotes.text: Copilot is a discovery interface for your existing authorization graph. Whatever a user can reach through normal access rules, copilot can summarize, correlate, and surface at conversational speed.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear explanation that Copilot reveals existing permission problems rather than creating new ones.

quotes.text: Agents are a control plane expansion. They widen the set of things that can be asked, found and done.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines why agent governance is an identity and execution problem, not just a content one.

Identity, ownerless resources and Power Platform
Control patterns and a unified governance layer

takeaways: Configuration is not control: Microsoft 365 governance only exists where enforcement is continuous, cross-service and backed by consequences.
Enforced ownership, lifecycle and risk-based prioritization are the primitives that keep sprawl, sharing drift and ownerless resources from becoming permanent.
Copilot and agents do not create new risk but expose and accelerate existing permission drift, so permissions must be baselined before AI scales them.
hook: Your Microsoft 365 tenant keeps creating teams, sites, flows and agents faster than any review process can keep up. This episode is for admins, architects and security leads who want to understand why policies on paper do not equal control. You get the five erosion patterns of tenant decay and the control patterns — ownership, lifecycle and risk-based consequence — that make governance predictable.
